metadata.purpose: label-shuffle leakage detector: gallery<->probe identity correspondence derangement-scrambled within every training batch, so training receives no genuine identity signal; everything else (images, architecture, loss, eval protocol) identical to the real pipeline.
metadata.note: This checkpoint is NOT a real result and is not saved under level1-features/results/.

randomized_tie_break_10_trials.purpose: rule out that above-chance recall is an artifact of deterministic argsort tie-breaking on a collapsed/near-constant embedding space
randomized_tie_break_10_trials.conclusion: unchanged from default tie-break (0.0181) -- not a tie-breaking artifact

untrained_random_init_control.purpose: isolate whether the above-pure-chance signal comes from the 5 epochs of scrambled-label training, or is simply the architecture's generic (untrained) response to real iris texture
untrained_random_init_control.conclusion: an UNTRAINED random-init model scores HIGHER (R@10=0.041) than the shuffle-trained model (R@10=0.018) on the identical real test protocol. This proves the above-chance signal is an architecture-only prior (circular conv filters respond somewhat to real iris texture even with zero training -- a known, benign effect for CNN features in metric learning/retrieval), present with or without any training, and is NOT something learned from the scrambled identity labels. Garbage-label training in fact makes it slightly WORSE than doing nothing, consistent with genuine embedding collapse under a meaningless loss signal.

followup_controls.final_verdict: Recall collapses from 0.7437 (real, correctly-labeled training) to 0.0181 (scrambled labels) -- a 41x drop -- and the small residual above the pure-independent-random floor (0.0050) is fully explained by an architecture-only prior unrelated to training labels, not by any leakage path in the split/eval pipeline. Check 5 PASSES.
